title: Where Saharan Dust Ends Up
geography: Sahara Desert to the Amazon basin

source.name: Yu et al., satellite study of trans-Atlantic Saharan dust transport

notes: Of the roughly 182 million tons lifted off the Sahara annually, NASA's study estimated about 27.7 million tons survives the roughly 5,000-mile crossing to settle over the Amazon basin; the remainder settles over the Atlantic Ocean and Caribbean en route. Recalled from the published study; not live-refreshed this run because outbound network access was unavailable in this session.

points.label: Settles over the ocean en route
